messages:
incident-bot: Pager -> HIGH: StratfordBank (enterprise - VPC, dedicated pool) experiencing surge of 500 errors on inference routes. Impact: customer-facing latency + retries. Possible need to pull request logs for 2026-03-15 20:00-20:20 UTC for forensic. @ryan_oncall listed as primary. :rotating_light:
Ryan (oncall): Got it. I'm on the call. Seeing error spikes from pool 'stratford-dedicated-1' and lots of 502/503 coming through the gateway. Trying a quick routing fallback to model-small to reduce traffic to the heavy variant.
Amar (SRE): Ryan — if we need raw request/response logs from the VPC connector they may contain PII (user messages). What's the ask from CS/legal before we pull full logs?
Maya (CSM): Customer is in an active compliance window and their security team has asked us not to share raw text. They asked us to investigate but avoid exporting any customer data unless legally approved. I asked them for specifics but no legal hold yet.
Sophia (Legal): If you think logs will contain PII, we need a documented exception. Minimal exposure principle: scope time window, maintain chain-of-custody, use ephemeral access, and redact where possible. I can approve a scoped, auditable access for incident response — need: justification, precise time range, list of people, and where the data will be stored.
Ryan (oncall): Understood. Operational ask: I need at least request/response metadata (status, latency, model variant, tenant id) + a redacted sample of payloads for the 20min window. Can we run a script that tokenizes sensitive fields (emails, cc numbers) rather than full export?
Kim (Infra): We can run the log extract job with the redaction pipeline enabled. Two options: (1) run with full redact=true which strips common PII patterns (emails, cc, ssn patterns) and returns placeholders; (2) run with raw=true but put results in an encrypted S3 bucket with extremely limited IAM and audit logs. Option 1 is fastest and lower risk.
Amar (SRE): For debugging we often need at least the full text of a single failing request to reproduce. Can we do a two-step: redacted bulk + one raw sample under legal hold?
Sophia (Legal): I can approve one raw sample if it's strictly scoped. Requirements: (a) sample must be pulled only by named people (list below), (b) stored in customer-specific encrypted bucket, (c) deleted after triage, (d) retention audit entry in the incident timeline. Please add justification and sign-off in this thread.
Maya (CSM): I'll get the customer's formal sign-off for the sample. They want engineers to try a config rollback first and only then share raw sample.
Ryan (oncall): Plan: 1) Canary rollback of routing to model-small on 10% traffic (now). 2) Run redacted log extract for 20:00-20:20 UTC with redact=true and post results here. 3) If redacted logs don't reproduce, request one raw sample under Sophia's sign-off.
deploy-bot: Canary rollback started: route-change-id=rc-7732, traffic-split=10% -> model-small. ETA 30s.
Ryan (oncall): Canary looks healthy so far, latency dropping. Still seeing a cohort of 502s from a few client IPs. Pulling redacted extract now.
Amar (SRE): Guidance for redaction job: use pipeline flag `--pii-filter=common` + `--window=\"2026-03-15T20:00:00Z/2026-03-15T20:20:00Z\"` and output to `s3://redwood-incident-temp/stratford/2067532100/redacted/`. Example command:

```
redwood-log-export \
  --tenant=stratfordbank --pool=stratford-dedicated-1 \
  --window=\"2026-03-15T20:00:00Z/2026-03-15T20:20:00Z\" \
  --pii-filter=common --output=s3://redwood-incident-temp/stratford/2067532100/redacted/ \
  --audit-note=\"incident 2067532100 - redacted export for triage\"
```

Amar (SRE): Note: `--pii-filter=common` covers emails, phone, cc patterns but not freeform personal data in messages.
Sophia (Legal): Confirming sign-off for the redacted export. For raw sample sign-off I need: list of personnel who will access (max 4), exact filename/path, and confirmation that customer CS will approve.
Maya (CSM): Customer approves redacted export. They will give limited sign-off for a single raw sample only if rollback doesn't fix it. I asked them to send an email to legal with acceptance.
Ryan (oncall): Nominate access list for raw sample: Ryan (oncall), Amar (SRE), Kim (Infra), and Sophia (Legal) to access if needed. Will add the email from customer once received.
Sophia (Legal): I tentatively approve that list. Final approval after customer email and a short justification snippet from Ryan on why redacted logs are insufficient. Keep the sample window to at most 3 requests.
Amar (SRE): Pulled redacted extract. Results: majority of failures show gateway timeouts to backend model process around 100-200ms beyond threshold, and 3 requests include long prompt that looks like transfer confirmations (possible PII) but were redacted to `<REDACTED>`. Uploading manifest now to the bucket.
Kim (Infra): Manifest: s3://redwood-incident-temp/stratford/2067532100/redacted/manifest.json (ACL=private, server-side-encryption=AES256). Audit event logged.
Ryan (oncall): Based on redacted sample, rollback eliminated most 502s. Customer CS says they still see a couple of failed transactions they want investigated. Requesting the one raw sample per process to reproduce locally. Maya — did customer send the email?
Maya (CSM): Customer email to legal received: "We authorize Redwood to provide one raw request sample under the controls discussed for incident triage." Forwarded to Sophia.
Sophia (Legal): Received. Final sign-off granted for up to 3 raw requests (max) in the specified window. Conditions: use ephemeral access creds (aws sts session), store in `s3://redwood-incident-legal/stratford/2067532100/raw/`, encrypt with customer CMK, and delete after 7 days unless legal hold. All access must be logged.
Amar (SRE): Performing controlled export for 3 raw requests now. Will attach hashed filenames and audit entries.
Amar (SRE): Export complete. Files: `raw-req-1.json`, `raw-req-2.json`, `raw-req-3.json` in the legal bucket. Access granted only to the four named people via temporary session tokens.
Ryan (oncall): I reproduced the failure locally using raw-req-2. It contains a long concatenated prompt causing KV cache growth and OOM on the model instance. Root cause tracks to a client-side retry loop that concatenates previous messages. Fix path: patch retry logic at the gateway, add input-length guard, and add a soft quota per-request.
Maya (CSM): Customer notified. They requested confirmation that raw data will be deleted after triage.
Sophia (Legal): Confirmed — if no legal hold, raw files will be deleted by 2026-03-22 and full deletion audit posted here. Marking this as approved incident exception.
Ryan (oncall): Patch for gateway retry logic is pushed to canary. Will schedule a full rollout after monitoring window.
deploy-bot: Deploy canary: gateway-retry-fix v1.0.1 -> traffic=5% (rc=7740).
Amar (SRE): Monitoring 30m post-deploy. Early telemetry looks good, error rate down to baseline. Creating an incident timeline entry with links to redacted manifests and legal approval emails.
Sophia (Legal): Please add the customer email and my sign-off text to the incident doc. Also include the S3 paths and the IAM principals who accessed raw files.
Ryan (oncall): Will do. Thanks everyone. Closing active pager but keeping thread open for retention/delete confirmation. :white_check_mark:
